sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. p. e1 (Japanese intro, scanned image, read visually) gives only the phoneme inventory (a i u e o, long and nasal vowels; k kh g gh c ch j jh retroflexes, aspirates, glottal stop etc.) and transcription conventions; no mention of accent/stress; body is glossed text.

sources.citation: KAKEN project pages 26370475 (Kobayashi, 'Complexification in the South Asian languages in hill areas', 2014-2017) and 18H00672 (Osada/Kobayashi/Badenoch, 'Documentation of endangered languages in Munda', 2018-2022), NII.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; final report of 18H00672 states Kobayashi 'has almost finished writing a grammar of Korwa. We have a plan to publish it near future'; outputs listed are the three eTULIP folk-tale texts and a 2017 talk 'The past suffixes of Hill Korwa'. Kobayashi's researchmap list (to 2025) shows no published Korwa grammar yet.

sources.citation: Anderson, Gregory D. S. (ed.). 2008. The Munda Languages (Routledge Language Family Series). London: Routledge. Publisher preview, pp. i-58 (Introduction + start of Santali chapter).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Korwa/Korowa/Koraku appear only in the classification table and history of research (Crooke 1892, Bahl 1962); no Korwa stress statement in the accessible pages. The Kherwarian chapter (Anderson, Osada & Harrison, pp. 195-255), which treats Korowa briefly, is not in the preview (archive.org copy is lending-restricted; full-text-inside API refused).

sources.citation: Kobayashi, Masato, Ganesh Murmu & Toshiki Osada. 2003. Report on a preliminary survey of the dialects of Kherwarian languages. Journal of Asian and African Studies (ILCAA, Tokyo) 66: 331-364.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Not about Korwa: covers Santali, Mundari and Ho only (12 informants); it has a section 1.2 'Word accent' for those three languages (image-only PDF, contents page read). Listed here because it is the same author's Kherwarian phonetic work; no Korwa data.

sources.citation: Bahl, Kali Charan. 1962. Korwa Lexicon (ms., 148 pp.), as digitized in Donegan, P. & D. Stampe 2004, Munda Lexical Archive, file 'Korwa'.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; segmental phonemic headwords with glosses, no prosodic marking, no introduction.

sources.citation: Konow, Sten [in Grierson, G. A. (ed.)]. 1906. Linguistic Survey of India, vol. IV: Munda and Dravidian languages. Calcutta: Office of the Superintendent of Government Printing. 'Korwa' section, pp. 148-166 (grammar sketch pp. 149-151 + specimens).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The Korwa sketch has only a 'Pronunciation' paragraph (palatal nasal retention, v ~ l correspondence, semi-consonants inconsistently marked); unlike the Santali (p. ~41 'Accent.—In words of two syllables the accent usually rests on the first..') and Mundari (p. 85 'The accent is the same as in Santali') sections, there is no 'Accent' paragraph for Korwa.

sources.citation: Anderson, Gregory D. S., Toshiki Osada & K. David Harrison. 2008. Ho and the other Kherwarian languages. In G. D. S. Anderson (ed.), The Munda Languages, 195-255. London: Routledge.

sources.note: Contains the short notes on Korowa (Korwa) and Koraku based on Bahl's materials and LSI; may carry a phonology/stress remark or an explicit 'as in Mundari' statement; also the standard citable secondary source.

sources.citation: Bahl, Kali Charan. n.d. [c. 1960-62]. A grammar and glossary of Korwa. Unpublished manuscript, University of Chicago Munda Languages Project (listed in Stampe's Munda bibliography, #R721; the 148-pp 'Korwa Lexicon' 1962 is its glossary part).
